The earliest specific institutional smoking ban in the retrieved evidence is the U.S. Senate's chamber ban, unanimously agreed to on March 9, 1914 [d5]. At the city level, Aspen, Colorado became the first U.S. city to require smokefree restaurants in 1987, and San Luis Obispo, California became the first city in the world to eliminate smoking in all public buildings — including bars and restaurants — in 1990 [d6][d3]. At the national level, Ireland was the first country in the world to pass a comprehensive "smoke-free law" on 29 March 2004, banning smoking in all indoor workplaces, restaurants, and bars, according to the WHO [d7][d9]. In the United Kingdom, smoking was banned in all public places across the entire country in 2007, when England became the final region to have the legislation come into effect [d2].
